title: Nebula Finance - POC scoping / workload modeling
summary: Discovery / POC scoping to agree success criteria and traffic model. Customer wants low-latency summarization + financial QA, is considering Dedicated vs Hosted. Main asks: target SLOs, expected QPS patterns, token distributions, benchmark plan and timeline. Agreed: run a 1-week benchmark on dedicated nodes, Redwood to share SOC2 + network diagram and provide an initial sizing and pricing sheet.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Alex Kim (Redwood), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Nebula), Marcus Vell (Head of AI), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Ivy Cho (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Discussed POC scope, workload characterization, QPS/concurrency, token distributions, and benchmarking timeline. Action items assigned.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. quick intro — Priya our SE will dig into the sizing.
00:07 Lena: Hi thanks, appreciate you fitting this in. we want to scope a POC around our transaction summarization and quick financial QA flows.
00:15 Priya: Great, quick Q — can you describe current traffic shape, QPS, and typical request/response size?
00:22 Marcus: Sure, right now our staging has pretty low QPS, like 3 to 5 qps during the day, but production spikes to 20 to 25 qps during batch windows, and we see bursty peaks up to 60 qps for short windows. concurrency per worker is roughly 8 to 12.
00:38 Jordan: OK that's helpful. is that for the summary flow or the QA flow?
00:41 Marcus: mostly summaries. the QA flow is heavier — it's retrieval augmented, so input includes a doc chunk plus a prompt; input token counts run higher.
00:50 Priya: Do you have token distributions? median / p95?
00:53 Marcus: rough numbers: summaries median input ~60 tokens, median output ~40 tokens. p95 output ~120 tokens. QA flow median input ~180 tokens because of the retrieved context, output ~90 tokens.
01:06 Samir: to add, about 40% of traffic is short summaries, 30% QA, 20% embeddings for search indexing, 10% ad-hoc analytics queries.
01:17 Priya: That helps a lot. For sizing we usually model QPS by workload: summaries 12 qps baseline, QA 8 qps baseline, embeddings 4 qps, with concurrency factors. Any strict latency SLOs?
01:28 Lena: Our product needs summary latency under 400 ms for 95th in interactive flows. For batch / offline it's okay to be higher, but online UX needs snappy responses.
01:35 Jordan: Understood. 400 ms p95 is tight but doable with the right model profile and dedicated capacity + batching/caching. we'll need to pick a model that trades off cost vs latency.
01:44 Marcus: We're also curious about cost. dedicated vs hosted — what's the delta for these profiles?
01:48 Priya: Good question. In general hosted is easiest — pay per token. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and often lower unit cost at scale. For your 20–25 qps sustained with bursts to 60, dedicated makes sense for predictability, and we can provision autoscale headroom for the bursts.
01:59 Alex: Also caching and prefix caching for repeated prompts can dramatically reduce tokens for summaries — that could shave cost and latency.
02:06 Samir: On security: we'll need VPC peering or private link and customer-managed KMS. SOC 2 compliance is required.
02:13 Jordan: We will share SOC 2 docs and our network diagram. Redwood Private is an option if you need on-prem, but often VPC + dedicated capacity suffices.
02:20 Marcus: Great. Let's talk benchmarking — how do you propose we run a realistic test?
02:24 Priya: We like a two-phase benchmark: first a synthetic workload that matches your token distributions and QPS to validate latency and throughput, then a real replay using anonymized production traces if you can provide them. We'll run both on a Redwood Dedicated trial cluster and also one run on Hosted to compare unit cost and latencies.
02:40 Lena: How long does the benchmark need to run?
02:43 Priya: Typically 3–7 days to capture traffic variability; for your case I'd recommend a 1-week run to hit burst windows.
02:49 Jordan: Timeline-wise we can provision dedicated trial capacity within 3 business days after we get the sample payloads and network ok. Then run the week-long benchmark and reconvene to review results — so end-to-end about 3 weeks from kickoff.
03:02 Samir: any gotchas on sample formats? we have parquet logs and a small API dump.
03:06 Priya: Parquet or ndjson both fine — we just need anonymized request/response pairs and timestamps. If you can't share full responses, we can approximate output tokens.
03:16 Marcus: We can provide two weeks of logs stripped of PII, we'll get that to you.
03:20 Jordan: Awesome. On success criteria, what are you measuring? latency p95, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, and quality metrics for summaries?
03:28 Lena: Yes: p95 latency under 400 ms for interactive, throughput to handle 25 qps sustained with bursts to 60, and summary accuracy measured vs our golden set with >0.85 ROUGE-type score. Also we need to validate security controls.
03:40 Priya: We'll instrument traces and advise on model selection — smaller quantized variants for low-latency, larger models or ensembles for quality. We'll log token counts and provide recommended batching configs and KV cache settings.
03:55 Jordan: For risk mitigation, we can set up fallback models if the low-latency model fails quality checks; autoscale will handle load spikes.
04:02 Marcus: Pricing sensitivity — what's the quick ballpark cost difference between hosted and dedicated for our profile?
04:06 Jordan: Ballpark: hosted might be higher per-token; for your sustained 25 qps + embeddings, dedicated with reserved capacity could be 30–40% cheaper at scale. We'll send a detailed sizing and pricing sheet.
04:18 Ivy: on compliance, do you have audit logs and RBAC for operators?
04:22 Alex: Yes we provide per-route logs, RBAC, SSO/SAML integrations, and full audit trail for Dedicated and Private. We'll include docs.
04:30 Samir: For benchmarking metrics, please capture concurrency, latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), token distribution by route, GPU utilization, and cost breakdown per route.
04:39 Priya: noted, that's our standard runbook. We'll also capture KV hit rates and batching stats since those impact cost.
04:47 Marcus: Any limitations with quantized models and retrieval context? sometimes kv cache doesn't play nicely with certain kernels.
04:52 Priya: There are cases where certain quantization levels change accuracy; we'll test a couple of quantization profiles and model variants. If needed we can do a fallback to float16 variants for QA.
05:03 Jordan: Next steps recap: Jordan send sizing/pricing and SOC2 + network diagram; Priya send benchmark runbook and infra checklist; customer provide anonymized logs and success criteria doc.
05:13 Lena: Sounds good. we'll aim to get logs by Friday and confirm kickoff.
05:18 Jordan: Great, I'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff and a shareable folder for artifacts.
05:23 Samir: One more thing — can you run a quick throughput test with our typical 180-token input and 90-token output to show baseline latency?
05:30 Priya: Yes we can, we usually run a sanity run against staging to validate tails. We'll include results in the kickoff.
05:37 Jordan: Any other questions?
05:39 Marcus: Not from us. looking forward to the run.
05:41 Jordan: Thanks everyone, meeting over.

End of transcript.
